source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Higher hemoglobin targets with ESAs can increase serious cardiovascular and thromboembolic risks","B":"Higher hemoglobin targets eliminate cardiovascular risk and are preferred whenever anemia is present","C":"ESA safety is unrelated to hemoglobin target, so dose escalation has no clinically important downside","D":"The only important ESA complication is hypoglycemia, which increases as hemoglobin approaches normal"}}
source_row.rationale: FDA boxed warnings for ESAs describe increased risks including death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and thromboembolism when used to target higher hemoglobin levels in CKD. Dosing should use the lowest dose sufficient to reduce transfusion needs.
source_row.source_detail: Boxed warning and CKD risk information for ESAs; cardiovascular, stroke, and thromboembolic risk with higher hemoglobin targets; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client with chronic kidney disease receives an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Why should an unnecessarily high hemoglobin target be avoided?
